newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr eases vs yen by Tokyo noon, awaits output data.
newsitem.headline: Dlr eases vs yen by Tokyo noon, awaits output data.

text.p: The dollar eased from earlier highs against the yen by Tokyo midday on Thursday due to a rise in Japanese government bond (JGB) yields.
"The dollar drifted lower against the yen as JGBs continued to be sold this morning," said a city bank trader.
The dollar, however, was underpinned by buying interest near Wednesday's New York low of 115.28 yen, dealers said.
At midday, the yield of the benchmark 182nd 10-year JGB stood at 2.735 percent, up from Wednesday's close of 2.685.

"The dollar slid lower as the market failed yesterday to push it decisively above the 200-day moving average, which lies slightly below 117.00 yen. However, there seems to be buying interest at around 115.30 yen," a trust bank trader said.
There was also talk of sporadic dollar buying by some U.S. players below 115.50 yen, dealers said.
Talk of option-related mark buy orders for yen at around 67.70/80 yen also helped to limit the dollar's downside versus the Japanese currency, dealers said.
Market participants were cautious ahead of the release of Japan's industrial production data for April at 0430 GMT, dealers said.
Economists polled by Reuters forecast rises in April output ranging from 0.3 percent to 1.5 percent, compared with month-on-month fall of 0.3 percent in March.
A higher-than-expected output rise could push the dollar below 115.00 yen in the afternoon, dealers said.
"We might see the dollar fall below 115.00 if the output data is strong. But only briefly as buying interest is likely to emerge," said the trust bank trader.
Dealers said movements in European currencies were likely to continue to have an influence on the dollar/yen's direction ahead of Sunday's final round of French National Assembly elections.

"A leftist victory in France would undermine the credibility of the future single European currency. This is bound to have a big impact on dollar/yen direction as well," said a trader at a foreign bank.
Rumours that a private poll showed the French Socialist party could win a clear majority knocked the dollar down against the mark overnight.
U.S. hedge funds strongly sold the dollar for the mark overnight, which made the dollar/mark direction unclear, a dealer at a European bank said.
The dollar's upside may be limited against the German and Japanese currencies if such activity continued, he added.
